high.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of July 22: ACB Leads Market at 7.8% p.a. for 12-Month Tenor; Big Four State Banks Hold at 6.8%
high.summary: ACB continues to lead Vietnam's deposit rate market, offering 7.8% p.a. for 12-month tenors, 7.7% for 9-month, and 7.6% for 6-month deposits. Saigonbank (7.2%) and Bac A Bank (7.1%) follow closely. Notably, PGBank has joined MBV, VCBNeo, and VIB in offering 7.0% p.a., bringing the total number of banks at or above this threshold to seven. The state-owned Big Four — Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, and VietinBank — remain unchanged at 6.8% p.a. for 12- and 18-month tenors, maintaining a 100 basis point spread below private sector leaders.

medium.title: Signs Confirming a Bottom for the VN-Index
medium.summary:
Financial analyst Huynh Hoang Phuong argues that one session of gains is insufficient to confirm a market bottom following the VN-Index's sharp decline of over 200 points. He identifies three key indicators investors should monitor: **time, valuation, and money flow**. On the time dimension, the current correction cycle — particularly when excluding heavyweights VIC and VHM — has been underway since early March 2026, now entering its fifth month. This is comparable in duration to the 2018 and 2022 bear cycles, which lasted approximately 3–4 quarters. While the correction has progressed significantly, the analyst suggests it may not yet be fully exhausted based on historical precedent. For international fund managers, this analysis is relevant for timing re-entry into Vietnamese equities. The emphasis on money flow (dòng tiền) as a confirmation signal is particularly pertinent — a sustained return of institutional and foreign capital would be a key leading indicator for VN-Index recovery and broader risk-on sentiment toward Vietnamese assets.

---

medium.title: Fluctuations in Real Estate Mortgage Lending Rates in the New Phase
medium.summary:
According to a market research report published by Dat Xanh Services Economic-Financial-Real Estate Research Institute (DXS-FERI), mortgage lending rates for real estate purchases in the first half of 2026 were commonly in the range of **12–14% per annum**, with some banks applying floating rates as high as **15–16.5% per annum**. Industry executives note that elevated borrowing costs are directly dampening buyer sentiment, with 70–80% of market transactions reportedly using leverage, making the secondary market particularly vulnerable to rate pressure. Developers are also facing increasingly difficult product absorption challenges. While this article focuses primarily on the real estate sector, the data point is **materially relevant for bond and rates traders**: lending rates at 12–16.5% signal a significantly tighter credit environment than prior cycles, suggesting either persistent SBV caution on monetary easing or structural liquidity tightness in the banking system. Investors should monitor whether these elevated rates reflect SBV policy signaling or individual bank liquidity stress — both carry implications for government bond demand and VND stability.

---

medium.title: A Banking Stock Unexpectedly Hits the Ceiling in the July 23 Session
medium.summary: In the afternoon session of July 23, banking stocks broadly reversed to trade in positive territory, with Sacombank (STB), Kienlongbank (KLB), and Nam A Bank (NAB) each gaining approximately 3%. Eximbank's stock (EIB) stood out, surging the maximum daily limit of 6.97% to VND 17,650/share with no sellers on the board. The catalyst appears to be the bank's upcoming Extraordinary General Meeting on July 24, where shareholders will vote on board-level personnel changes — including the dismissal and replacement of several Board of Directors members — with candidates already approved by the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV). The planned board composition of 7 members, including 6 independent directors, signals a potential governance overhaul. This broad banking sector rally on July 23 is a mildly positive signal for the VN-Index's financial sub-index, and the SBV's pre-approval of Eximbank board candidates indicates active regulatory oversight of banking sector governance.

medium.title: H1 2026 Bank Profit Disclosures: Techcombank Posts VND 18,540 Billion Pre-Tax Profit, Up 22.5% YoY — Leads Private Banking Sector
medium.summary: Techcombank reported strong H1 2026 results with pre-tax profit of VND 18,540 billion (+22.5% YoY), confirming its position as the leading private-sector bank by profitability. Total assets reached VND 1.273 quadrillion as of June 30, 2026, a 6.9% increase from year-end 2025. Credit growth on a standalone basis reached 14.3% YTD (11.6% excluding loans exempt from credit quotas), reflecting robust lending momentum. The loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR) edged down slightly to 80.1% from 80.5% in Q1, remaining well within SBV's 85% regulatory cap, while the short-term funding used for medium- and long-term lending stood at 27.8% against the 30% ceiling. Capital adequacy (CAR under Basel II) was 15.0%, marginally down from 15.2% in Q1 following a dividend payment. As 10 banks have now disclosed H1 results, the overall picture suggests resilient sector profitability, which is supportive for Vietnamese bank equities and broadly constructive for financial system stability — a key factor underpinning VND credit quality.
